EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development in the past 24 hours is the significant pause in US military strikes against Iran, following 13 consecutive days of attacks, driven by diplomatic efforts spearheaded by Oman and concerns over depleted US air defense stockpiles. Concurrently, an escalation of violence in the West Bank, including settler attacks and Israeli military operations, raises fears of a new intifada.

IRAN
The Iranian Foreign Ministry reported "productive" talks with Oman in Tehran on Friday and Saturday regarding the Strait of Hormuz, with progress made on safe shipping mechanisms, though the transit status remains unchanged. Iran strongly condemned Ukraine's attack on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, which resulted in one sailor killed and one injured, calling it an "act of aggression" that could escalate the war, and summoned Ukraine's Chargé d'Affaires. The Iranian Army spokesman claimed Iran's strikes forced the US to halt and revisit its regional strategy, and warned of "significantly increased" US casualties in any potential ground operation. The IRGC spokesman explicitly warned Britain, Israel, and Gulf States that they would become "legitimate and certain targets" if they supported US military operations. Press TV, citing the IRGC, claimed Iran destroyed 11 US military aircraft and helicopters at regional bases over two weeks (July 17-31). The Wall Street Journal (via Iranian channels) reported Iran's effective use of Kheibar Shekan ballistic missiles combined with drones to challenge US air defenses. Reports from Bandar Abbas indicated explosions, which Iranian sources later clarified were controlled demolitions of unexploded ordnance from previous US-Israeli attacks in Qeshm and Pakdasht. Iran's Supreme Council decided to remove YouTube and arrest "YouTube stars," citing "Zionist enemy engineering consciousness." An earthquake of 4.6 magnitude struck Kerman province. Local residents in the port city of Jask were reported to be patrolling with weapons, "awaiting American forces."

ISRAEL
Prime Minister Netanyahu announced he would speak with President Trump on Iran and stated Israel is "ready for broader action" in the West Bank. The Israeli cabinet meeting was held in a secure underground facility due to the security situation. The government authorized the army to mobilize 240,000 reservists until the end of September 2026. IDF forces sealed the home of the Palestinian attacker in Tell (Shomron) who carried out Friday's shooting that killed Maj Yuval Ezra (27) and Sgt Maj (res) Benayahu Mellet (32), ahead of its planned demolition. The homes of his two alleged accomplices, including the one who snatched a weapon, were also mapped for sealing and demolition. IDF operations in Gaza last week killed Fares al-Masri (Hamas weapons production chief), Mohammad Abu Shakian (Hamas Nukhba), Muhannad Asaad Mahmoud Abu Ghazal (Hamas Nukhba commander, involved in Oct 7 Kissufim raid), Raed Hani Mohammed (Hamas aerial surveillance), and Nabhan Mohammed Nabhan al-Amsi (Hamas Gaza City Brigade intelligence chief). Hamas also reported the killing of Wael al-Ladawi, its interior security chief in central Gaza, and officer Ramez Abu Zureiq in Deir al-Balah. A drone fell near the Hebron home of National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. Defense Minister Israel Katz reportedly met with administrative detainee Yinon Derdik, accused of abusing a Palestinian, who is on a hunger strike. Kan News reported that US air transport of aircraft and munitions to Israel is continuing despite the US pause in strikes against Iran. Opposition leader Benny Gantz's partner Gadi Eizenkot reportedly set a target of 63-64 Zionist MKs for the next Knesset, conditioned on a universal conscription law.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces killed several senior Hamas operatives in Gaza, including Fares al-Masri (Hamas weapons production), Mohammad Abu Shakian (Hamas Nukhba), Muhannad Asaad Mahmoud Abu Ghazal (Hamas Nukhba, Oct 7 Kissufim raid), Raed Hani Mohammed (Hamas aerial surveillance), and Nabhan Mohammed Nabhan al-Amsi (Hamas Gaza City Brigade intelligence chief). Hamas reported the killing of Wael al-Ladawi, its interior security chief in central Gaza, and officer Ramez Abu Zureiq. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers set fire to mosques in Qusra (near Nablus) and Kur (near Tulkarm), with "Revenge" and "Jewish blood is not free" graffiti. Two suspects were arrested for overnight arsons. Seven Palestinian suspects were arrested for an attack on an Israeli citizen at Moreno Farm near Beitar Illit. An Israeli man was wounded by a stone near Susya, where a Palestinian snatched his gun and fired it in the air before being apprehended. The IDF Central Command banned Palestinian workers from all Israeli communities in the West Bank. The defense establishment expressed concerns about a potential new intifada, noting a "barrier of fear broken among Palestinians." A rights group reported over 1,000 Palestinian children displaced in the West Bank this year. Hamas condemned US-Israeli measures targeting UNRWA. The Israeli military deployed five additional companies to the West Bank, arresting over 70 wanted individuals and interrogating hundreds.

LEBANON
Syrian President Ahmed a-Sharaa stated that Syria does not intend to intervene militarily in Lebanon, emphasizing a comprehensive approach to the crisis and supporting the Lebanese state's monopoly on weapons. A Hezbollah official threatened "full entry" into the conflict if Israel launched a direct attack on Iran. Israeli attacks in South Lebanon were reported.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Syrian President Ahmed a-Sharaa told Al-Jazeera that Syria is avoiding confrontation with Israel and is seeking a security agreement with Israel, with the participation of a group of countries. He also met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres. Syria reported a bus crash on the Damascus-Deir Ezzor road resulting in 35 deaths and 30 injuries. In Iraq, the Kurdistan region suffered 940 drone and missile attacks over the past four months, causing 32 deaths and over 150 injuries. An unidentified drone was reportedly shot down near the US Consulate in Erbil. A massive fire with continuous explosions erupted at the Jambur oil field in Kirkuk. Iraqi security forces removed all posters of Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei from Karbala. The US Embassy in Erbil issued a security warning due to recent Iranian strikes.

GULF STATES
Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on "sensitive" Saudi Aramco oil facilities in Jizan and Yanbu using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones. The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported an incident in the southern Red Sea where a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile. The Kuwaiti government approved a military and defense cooperation agreement with Pakistan. Politico reported growing rifts among Arab states regarding the conflict with Iran, noting divergent priorities and the UAE's earlier withdrawal from OPEC, leading to a "non-functional" GCC. However, Kuwait's Ambassador to Washington denied a Wall Street Journal report claiming Kuwaiti and Bahraini fighter jets participated in covert strikes on Iran, calling the claim "baseless" and denying permission for offensive operations from its territory. Yemeni forces claimed shooting down a Turkish-made Bayraktar Akıncı drone owned by Saudi Arabia over Al Jawf Province, where clashes between Houthis and local tribesmen killed 7 Houthi fighters and 3 tribesmen. Brigadier General Esmaeil Qa’ani, IRGC Quds Force Chief, demanded Saudi Arabia lift its 12-year blockade on Yemen.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Pause in Iran Strikes:** President Trump ordered a pause in US military strikes against Iran on Friday, ending a 13-day streak, citing an ongoing diplomatic window and concerns about dangerously depleted US Patriot missile interceptor stockpiles in the Middle East.
2.  **West Bank Escalation:** Violence in the West Bank intensified with Israeli settler arsons on two mosques in Qusra and Kur, Hebrew graffiti, and an incident near Susya where an Israeli civilian was wounded and his weapon snatched. Israel’s defense establishment expressed concerns about a potential "Intifada."
3.  **Caspian Sea Attack:** Ukraine claimed responsibility for an attack on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, killing one sailor and injuring another. Iran condemned the attack as an "act of aggression" that could escalate the regional conflict.
4.  **Hormuz Diplomacy:** Iran reported "productive" talks with Oman in Tehran regarding the safe passage of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, with consultations ongoing.
5.  **Senior Hamas Commanders Killed:** IDF operations in Gaza killed several high-ranking Hamas operatives, including Fares al-Masri (weapons production), Muhannad Asaad Mahmoud Abu Ghazal (Nukhba, Oct 7 Kissufim raid), and Wael al-Ladawi (interior security chief in central Gaza).
6.  **IRGC Threats to Allies:** The IRGC spokesman warned the UK, Israel, and Gulf States that they would become "legitimate targets" if they supported US military operations against Iran.
7.  **Saudi Aramco Facilities Targeted:** Yemen's Houthis claimed to have attacked "sensitive" Saudi Aramco oil facilities in Jizan and Yanbu with drones and missiles.
8.  **Kuwait Denies Iran Strikes:** Kuwait's Ambassador to Washington explicitly denied a Wall Street Journal report claiming Kuwaiti and Bahraini fighter jets participated in covert operations against Iran.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation remains critically high despite the US pause in strikes against Iran. Flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where US naval blockade enforcement continues alongside diplomatic efforts, and the Caspian Sea, now a new front following Ukraine's attack on an Iranian vessel. Iran's explicit warnings to the UK, Israel, and Gulf States, combined with Hezbollah's threat of full involvement if Israel directly attacks Iran, signal a potential for broader conflict. The escalating violence in the West Bank, marked by settler attacks and military deployments, raises the specter of a new "Intifada," posing an internal security threat to Israel. The Houthis' continued attacks on Saudi Arabian oil facilities and Red Sea shipping present a persistent maritime security risk, potentially disrupting global energy supplies. President Trump's declaration that he is "absolutely" considering a full return to military conflict if US demands are not met underscores the fragile nature of the current de-escalation.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture shifted dramatically with President Trump's decision to pause strikes against Iran, influenced by diplomatic progress with Oman and concerns over depleting Patriot missile interceptor stockpiles. However, Trump warned he is considering resuming "full-scale war" if Iran does not meet "100% of what we want." CENTCOM confirmed its naval blockade remains active. **Oman**, along with **Qatar**, has been actively mediating, proposing a return to pre-July 9 positions for de-escalation. **Ukraine** claimed a significant long-range strike on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea, which it alleges was transporting military supplies to Russia, deepening its involvement in the Iran-Russia axis of evil narrative. Ukraine also accused Russia of providing satellite intelligence to Iran for its regional attacks. **Russia** continued missile attacks on Kyiv and is reportedly seeking 30,000 additional North Korean troops and more ballistic missile launchers. The **UK** was specifically warned by Iran's IRGC spokesman that it would become a "legitimate target" if it supported US operations. **Germany** is treating a car ramming attack at a Berlin Pride event, which killed one and injured 16, as suspected terrorism, with the suspect linked to Islamist activity. **Syria's** President a-Sharaa emphasized avoiding confrontation with Israel and seeking a security agreement, while also stating Syria would not intervene militarily in Lebanon. **Kuwait** formally denied participating in any military operations against Iran, contradicting Wall Street Journal reports.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions emerged regarding Gulf states' involvement in operations against Iran, with Kuwait's Ambassador to Washington explicitly denying a Wall Street Journal report that Kuwaiti and Bahraini jets attacked Iran. There is also a discrepancy in reporting regarding the scale of US preparations, with some Israeli sources claiming readiness for a "major US attack" while US sources (Barak Ravid) suggested preparations were for attacks of similar scale to previous nights. Unverified claims include the IRGC's assertion of destroying 11 US aircraft and helicopters and Ukraine's detailed claims of targeting specific vessels in the Caspian Sea (which Iran describes as a commercial vessel). The claim by Omid Dana of Tehran preventing six commercial/oil ships from passing Hormuz in the last 24 hours is notable but uncorroborated by other sources. Propaganda indicators are prevalent across the board, from Press TV's explicit framing of Western media reports to the White House's use of Katy Perry's song in a strike video and the IRGC spokesman's strong, declarative warnings. Reporting gaps exist concerning the specific details of the Oman-Iran agreement on Hormuz, the precise nature and timing of alleged Israeli strikes in South Lebanon, and independent verification of the full extent of Houthi and other proxy attacks.
